summary: LDAP field-level privacy is configured and persists across serial restarts of both nodes. The supplied HR record remains intact, remote reader/admin access works over LDAPS, and the OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL 9-compatible 389 Directory Server on node1 and LDAP clients on both nodes.
Loaded the supplied HR LDIF and retained it at /srv/legacy2/ldap-attribute-privacy/hr.ldif.
Created dedicated directory-reader and hr-admin identities with node-generated credentials stored in root-only credential files.
Restricted the reader to employee names and mail; employeeNumber cannot be read, searched, or modified by the reader.
Allowed the HR administrator to read and modify employeeNumber; restored the demonstration value to HR-4815.
Confirmed anonymous searches return no employee records.
Restarted node1 and node2 serially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Supplied HR records loaded and retained
evidence.summary: Shows Morgan loaded in LDAP and the original LDIF retained with its contents and checksum.

evidence.requirement: Reader can search names and mail from node2 but cannot access employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Reader receives cn and mail only, cannot filter on employeeNumber, and modification is rejected with LDAP error 50.

evidence.requirement: Only HR administrator can administer employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Administrator reads, changes, and restores employeeNumber; final value is HR-4815.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous users see no employee records
evidence.summary: Anonymous employee result count is zero before and after restarts.
Credentials were generated on-node and retained as root-owned mode-0600 files for reader and administrator demonstrations.
Both nodes remain on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64.
Captures healthy baseline, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered LDAP service/data, and remote privacy behavior.
Captures healthy baseline, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, persisted credentials/client, and recovered remote LDAP access.
